surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Cooley lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Logan Cooley got the scoring started for the Mammoth early in the first, and he struck again midway through the period to make it 2-0. Erik Karlsson got the Penguins on the board midway through the second. Rickard Rakell tied it up shorthanded midway through the third, and Ben Kindel put the Pens ahead 3-2 with 25 seconds left. With the goalie pulled and just one second left, Cooley completed his hat trick to tie it 3-3. Mikhail Sergachev won it in overtime.
The Mammoth had a bit more of the good stuff. The Penguins hit two posts and came up a goal short. Sebastian Cossa made 31 saves for the Mammoth, and Artūrs Šilovs stopped 30 of 34 at the other end.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Mammoth moved to 9-5-0, second in the Central, while the Penguins dropped to 5-6-2, sixth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Evgeni Malkin passed Nicklas Lidström for 24th on the NHL’s all-time assists list, with 879.
Mikhail Sergachev has a point in six straight games.
Erik Karlsson extended his point streak against Utah to six games.
The Mammoth’s Artem Duda played his first NHL game.
